key: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
s: Against deniers who dismiss the revelations as old fables, the chapter gives its answer; al-Tabari, on 83:12 to 83:14, reads the rust as sins that overpower the heart, flood it and close round it until they cover it, as wine overpowers the mind.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 83:12 to 83:14, the Tarteel QUL text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: يقول: غلب على قلوبهم وغَمَرها وأحاطت بها الذنوب فغطتها، يقال منه: رانت الخمر على عقله، فهي تَرِين عليه رَيْنا، وذلك إذا سكر، فغلبت على عقله
evidence.gloss: He says: the sins overpowered their hearts, flooded them and closed round them, and so covered them; one says of it, ‘the wine rana over his mind’, it covers it over, and that is when he is drunk and it overpowers his mind.
evidence.licence: classical text public domain; digitisation by Tarteel (QUL), no licence stated; short excerpt with attribution

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Mutaffifin 83:14, at 5861). In his single comment on 83:12 to 83:14 al-Tabari glosses rana in his own voice: sins overpowered the hearts, flooded them, closed round them and covered them, and gives the usage of the verb for wine overpowering a drunkard’s mind, then says the exegetes and the report from the Prophet (the black spot hadith) agree. The sentence paraphrases his gloss; the wine clause reproduces his lexical parallel, not an added moral. Plain sense faithful: 83:13 has the denier call the revelations fables of the men of old and 83:14 opens with the rebuttal Nay. entry-check ok.
